Go classpath entries accept directories, archives or mounted fs.FS resources; general JVM providers/manifest expansion/module-loader hooks remain separate. DistributedServerFiles delegates to the same resolver, and RMI caches actual TLAFile objects with pre-write URI timing rather than bare strings. Production config/parser file reads use GetPath. All eight upstream SimpleFilenameToStreamTest cases are ported after implementation using existing test_vectors/ fixtures; the Windows case keeps its source platform guard. Actual Java-source probes match provenance, archive URIs, Unicode/space URI spelling, search descriptions, overrides, suffixes and archive predicates. The full workspace passes offline and real worker file/tool/bootstrap probes pass under -race. Network registry/export/RPC and complete worker command lifecycle remain pending.
- Local worker group/bootstrap now follows Java post-lookup startup: FP64 is initialized from the server before fresh source-backed interning and config/tool creation; the server supplies the CLI deadlock flag independently of CHECK_DEADLOCK, preprocess=true and current polynomial. One shared runtime/latch/executor hosts indexed registration runnables, workers publish before registration, all threads start before timer/readiness, and readiness does not wait for registration. Keepalive/shutdown read live runnable workers. Local canonical-host lookup retains address preference, reverse/forward verification, numeric IPv6 spelling, five-second cache, and UnknownHost cause wrapping, using Go native resolution; JVM resolver providers/hosts-file/general TTL/scoped-address/security hooks remain pending. Distributed Integer.getInteger properties now decode Java signs/hex/octal/BMP digits with signed bounds and invalid fallback. FP64 uses Java Random, has typed index bounds and separate unrolled/loop integer extensions; polynomial 65 now has Java’s missing hex digit restored. Ported upstream FP64Test after implementation. All 131 constants and 655 Java-source extension pairs match; 24 Java Integer.decode cases, real parser/file/tool group bootstrap, canonical hostname and concurrent group race probe pass. Full offline workspace checks pass with external config-test edits preserved. Registry lookup/retry, endpoint export/RPC and full worker command/error/exit wiring remain pending; persistent fixtures continue to use test_vectors/.
- UniqueString interning now uses a concrete Java-style InternTable: linear probing/String hashes, growth before cache lookup, signed token increments, live slot scans, remote-source tokens/locations without advancing the local counter, cause-free interning assertions for Exceptions, and Error escape. Worker loading installs a fresh source before creating config/tool values, refreshes cached names, and copies master replies so locations remain independent. Checkpoints now write slot order and recover into the existing table with duplicates/growth; incomplete records raise Java’s nullable corruption assertion. Server checkpointing includes interner begin/commit at Java’s positions and leaves pre-resume failures suspended. Existing Java record/deep-copy initialization tests now use their actual isolated InternTable(2). Java/Go byte and slot probes and a concurrent race probe passed; offline full workspace checks pass with pending external edits preserved. Network registry/FP64/group startup and remaining general filename/archive APIs are still pending.
- Persistent TLC fixtures belong in tlc/test_vectors/, never tlc/testdata/. The user reserves testdata/ for ephemeral Go fuzzer storage and cleanup. The worker URI oracle vectors were renamed and their reader updated; preserve this rule for every later test port.
- Distributed worker file resolution and local server file transfer are now ported: basename-only server requests, packaged-model/spec/library/embedded-standard search, directory/size checks, single-read zero filling, and nested RuntimeException/IOException causes. The worker preserves its remote-only cache-miss fetch, ignored flags/library paths, deleted-file refetch, remote-failure empty files, null-byte exception timing, and UTF-16 GetFullPath separator quirk; iteration is deterministic InsMap order. Process-exit file cleanup is wired into the command wrapper. LoadDistributedWorkerTool uses configuration-first loading and the production parser/semantic checker/bridge for all remote modules. No Java tests target this resolver or getFile; temporary probes against the actual Java resolver and Go production loading passed, and offline full workspace checks pass. Network bootstrap/remote interning, canonical-host/export discovery, and the general FilenameToStream/archive APIs remain pending.
- Worker URI metadata is now constructed and immutable: rmi://hostname:port/threadId is retained raw for registration/statistics/getURI, while failure messages use Java NFC and uppercase UTF-8 percent escapes. Java server-vs-registry authority classification, nullable host, bracketed IPv6/scope IDs, hostname/IPv4 rules, component masks, escapes, UTF-16 error indices and IllegalArgumentException -> URISyntaxException are represented for the constructor-produced hierarchical URI. Local defaults use the machine hostname and port zero; DistributedWorkerAddress supplies a future exported endpoint. Unicode normalization uses cached golang.org/x/text v0.28.0, with a canonical fallback because its stream-safe CGJ insertion differs from Java for long combining sequences. Genuine input CGJs remain intact. All 232 OpenJDK 21.0.12.1 fixtures and the rejection-message integration check pass; the full workspace suite passes offline. Java TLC has no dedicated URI test. Endpoint allocation/reflection/VM diagnostics/canonical-host lookup and worker resolver/bootstrap/registry transport remain pending.
- FP-manager execution and failover now mirror Java locally: registrations have distinct FPSets wrapper identity, cached hostnames and availability; reassignment keeps partition count, shares wrappers, preserves the non-wrapping replacement-loop quirk, and caches exhaustion. Scalar/block failures catch Exception but let Error escape, retry replacements, and use Java BitVector(size,true) on exhaustion. Parallel block tasks collect by saved partition index and preserve submission retry/shutdown rules; checkFPs/checkInvariant use completion collection too. Statistics failures reassign without retrying; duplicate partition counts and grouped close/checkpoint identity are preserved. Worker containsBlock and server putBlock use their shared executors, making sibling-worker rejection after exit observable. Empty distributed managers report zero and indexing throws ArithmeticException; non-distributed calls bypass executors and preserve IOException fallbacks. All nineteen DynamicFPSetManagerTest and five FPSetManagerTest cases are ported, including FaultyFPSet virtual dispatch and factory-created nested high-bit partitions with bounded memory. Full workspace checks and targeted race checks pass; a standalone shared-worker probe confirms ServerException -> RemoteException -> RejectedExecutionException after sibling exit. The subsequent URI port covers local metadata; worker resolver/startup/registry transport remains pending.
- Distributed worker exit now has a concrete local runtime representing one Java worker JVM: shared executor shutdown, keepalive cancellation, ordered worker group, and completion latch. Exit prints before shutdown/cancel/forced-unexport/countdown; repeated direct exits fail at unexport and do not count down again. Proxy calls after unexport return direct NoSuchObjectException while direct isAlive remains true. Runtime shutdown catches only direct NoSuchObjectException and keeps the executor/latch; awaiting termination retains the ten-second delay. Local keepalive preserves Java activity, timeout int overflow, server-done and ordered-exit behavior; source remote catches and exit warnings now cover server keepalive, final cache reads, and graceful cleanup. Invocation time and total-computation snapshots use atomics. The Go constructor gives a worker its own runtime; assemble a shared runtime before registration to model multiple threads in one JVM. The subsequent URI and FP-manager ports cover local metadata and connect the shared executors; resolver/startup/registry transport remains pending.
- Distributed worker registrations now use a single thread-identity-to-worker registry like Java's `threadsToWorkers`, protected for Go concurrent access and enumerated in insertion order. Repeated registrations (including equal URIs or the same worker object) create distinct threads; URI is display metadata rather than a key. Removal returns/removes only the selected thread's worker and emits a deregistration message once. Worker counts and block selectors use registry size; `GetNewStates` sums queue size plus every registered thread's assigned block length, including calls waiting at the worker. Registrations and state-count queries preserve Java's monitor serialization; worker `GetNextStates` is also serialized. Worklist references use atomic publication for timer/progress readers, and keepalive starts during construction before `Start`. Final join/statistics/exit handling removes registrations quietly in Java order. Full existing checks pass in the current workspace; no tests were added or modified. Sent/received counters retain Java int overflow; result/statistics/timestamp processing stays inside the remote/NPE catch, so null results/first partitions deregister the worker while empty first partitions reach the outer model-error catch. Worker exit/export lifecycle and URI ASCII/NFC metadata remain to port.
- Value-stream parity now includes strong object references in the output identity table, null handles, Java input-table capacity/index/assignment behavior, and `GetValue`'s UniqueString cast. `WriteExternal` shares Java's ordinary wire format: external safety is the reader discarding saved string tokens/locations and re-interning, not a writer replacing them with -1. Compact natural writes keep Java's unchecked, comment-only non-negative precondition. Null cached-value writes throw NPE; dummy set caches use one null-ValueVec sentinel whose handle and kind byte are written before failure. Unsupported values/kinds preserve WrongInvocationException text and signed byte diagnostics. File-stream truncated reads produce nullable EOFExceptions compatible with Go EOF recovery; bad array lengths, indices, and handle casts preserve typed runtime failures. Byte-queue state reads now skip handle tracking and preserve array-index failures instead of file-style EOF. Model-value stream reads use the already-initialized global table without silently building it. Full existing checks pass in the current workspace; no tests were added or modified.
- Value string APIs now mirror Java's checked/unchecked and delimiter overloads through `ValueToString`, `StringWithDelimiter`, and `StringUnchecked`. Concrete `ToString` buffer methods retain nested flags and offsets without entering each child's public wrapper. Public string conversion adds Java's separate source catch. Optional buffer interfaces retain compatibility with foreign Go values/user objects that implement only `String`. Lazy expansion catches preserve shared partial output and rethrow in unchecked mode; product printers keep expanded printing outside their materialization catch, `UNION` does not swallow expansion errors, and function lambdas always swallow expansion/printing failures and print their materialized function in checked mode. Predicate-set symbolic domains and function parameter domains still enter checked public string conversion. `TLC!Print`, `PrintT`, and `ToString` now use unchecked conversion, including the newline inside `PrintT`'s file-output pretty-print input. Full existing checks pass in the current workspace; no tests were written or modified for this port.
- The latest user instruction is feature-first Java parity, then port that feature's Java tests when they exist. This supersedes the earlier no-new-tests phase. Do not translate tests for a feature before its Go implementation.
- The mixed-set config test now checks the raw parsed elements and Java's comparison failure during normalization for printing. The reported remote Linux panic reproduces locally with the committed test; local green runs used the uncommitted correction. A temporary bundled-Java ModelConfig probe confirms the raw three-element unnormalized set and the same boolean/string comparison failure. The correction passes 100 uncached repetitions, 100 repetitions under -race, and the full offline go test ./... without a skip. Preserve production Java behavior; no new test was added. Persistent fixtures use test_vectors/, never testdata/.
- Keep the Go code mostly in package `tlc`, prefer concrete structs over interfaces, and use `InsMap` whenever deterministic iteration matters.
- Recent upstream Java TLC history through `8f4bc8b73` was rechecked against Go for empty function/sequence equivalence, empty interval-domain function equality, interval arithmetic overflow, temporal negation normalization before liveness DNF, initial liveness evaluation errors, DiskStateQueue wake/suspend fixes, empty set-constructor enumeration/random selection, and `_POSSIBLE` unwitnessed diagnostics. Those fixes are already represented in Go; do not repeat that commit-by-commit audit unless upstream advances.
- No-code audit note: recent Java `_POSSIBLE` follow-ups, `TLCGet("revision").calver`, raw `ByteArrayQueue` `StateVec` reversal, and obvious map-iteration hazards were rechecked. Go already keeps `_Counts` at state level, avoids implicit periodic `_PrintCounts`, exposes `revision.calver`, preserves the raw byte-queue reverse packing, and uses `InsMap`, explicit side-order slices, or sorting on the checked user-visible map paths.
- DOT writer derived filenames must use Java `String.replace(".dot", ...)` semantics, replacing every occurrence rather than only a suffix or first match. This affects both snapshot filenames and liveness DOT filenames when a directory component also contains `.dot`.
- DiskFPSet `Sizeof` intentionally mirrors Java's approximate accounting, including 4-byte outer-table and index slots rather than Go pointer-width accounting. Preserve that raw MX/statistics shape instead of making it architecturally "more correct."
- Heap-backed `DiskFPSet.Put`/`Contains` now mirror Java's striped lock architecture instead of serializing through one Go mutex. Java's flusher relies on reentrant write locks by holding one stripe and acquiring all stripes again; Go preserves the effective exclusion by acquiring all stripes except the already-held stripe during flush. Do not replace this with `sync.RWMutex` recursive locking; Go mutexes are not reentrant. The BRAF fallback reader pool has its own mutex, and hit/seek/write counters use atomic increments like Java's `LongAdder`-style statistics.
- No-code inventory note: `IActionItemList`, `IContextEnumerator`, and `DiskFPSetMXBean` are Java interface-only surfaces represented by concrete Go `ActionItemList`, `ContextEnumerator`, and `DiskFPSetMXWrapper` methods. `InternRMI`, `TLCServerRMI`, `TLCWorkerRMI`, and `RMIFilenameToStreamResolver` remain Java RMI/spec-file-transfer transport surfaces outside the local checker core.
- Monolith `.tla` config extraction must pass Java's `configFileName.replace(".tla", "")` value to the marker matcher. That keeps the source-of-truth full-path behavior where `/tmp/Scratch.tla` looks for `CONFIG /tmp/Scratch`, not `CONFIG Scratch`.
- Simulator RL numeric system properties use Java `Double.valueOf` syntax, including optional `d`, `D`, `f`, or `F` suffixes. Keep Go property parsing aligned with that Java float-literal boundary.
- `TLCExt!TLCCache` constant-level caching is scoped by Java `Tool` id as well as expression identity. Go keeps a dedicated cache store keyed by `(Tool.ID, SemanticNode UID)` instead of reusing the single generic `SemanticNode.ToolObject`, because that slot is also used by coverage/action/debug metadata and Java's `getToolObject(tool.getId())` is per-tool.
- `TLC!TLCEval` constant-level caching follows the same Java per-tool boundary as `TLCExt!TLCCache`. Keep its cache in the dedicated `(Tool.ID, SemanticNode UID)` store and do not write cached values back to the shared `SemanticNode.ToolObject`, which is also used for definitions, coverage, actions, and debugger metadata.
- `TLCGet("spec")` constraint metadata is also per-tool like Java `getToolObject(toolId)`: `SpecProcessor` stores constraint `OpDefNode`s in the dedicated `(Tool.ID, SemanticNode UID)` store, and coverage later replaces that same per-tool slot with the constraint `Action`. Do not collapse constraints back into shared `SemanticNode.ToolObject`.
- IOUtils text `Serialize` must not create missing parent directories. Java delegates to `Files.writeString(Paths.get(...), ...)`, so parent-directory creation is limited to Java's JSON serializer paths and the trace-serialization boundary that explicitly creates parents.
- IOUtils argument validation uses Java's `TLC_MODULE_ONE_ARGUMENT_ERROR` boundary. Non-string tuple elements deliberately report operator name `IOExec` even for template/environment variants because frozen CommunityModules routes every element through `IOUtils.convert`.
- IOUtils process execution distinguishes Java `ProcessBuilder.start()` failures from real child-process exits: failed launches return an override error, while a started process with nonzero exit status returns the usual `{exitValue, stdout, stderr}` record.
- Coverage report gating mirrors Java's split behavior: checker/simulator cost models are created for global, action, or variable coverage, but periodic/final `CostModelCreator.report` output is emitted only when global interval coverage is enabled. Checker/DFID reports also keep Java's `tool.getActions().length > 0` guard; simulator reports do not add that guard.
- No-code audit note: `ModelChecker.modelCheckImpl`, `DoInitFunctor`, `Worker.run`, init-progress printing, and checker progress-stat reporting were rechecked against Java. Go preserves the no-action success-cleanup branch, init-state functor ordering, post-error successor suppression, worker nil-dequeue shutdown, deadlock/liveness tail flow after ordinary next-state errors, zero-init BFS success behavior, and Java double-to-long progress speed conversions.
- `MemFPSet`, `MemFPSet2`, `MultiFPSet`, and distributed FP-set collision-distance aggregation use Java signed-`long` distance/min behavior, including overflow quirks such as `Math.abs(Long.MIN_VALUE)`. Do not replace these with friendlier unsigned absolute distances; the values feed Java-visible success/collision diagnostics.
- Worker trace enumeration must stop at the worker trace file's current pointer, not physical file length. Java `Worker.Enumerator` captures `raf.getFilePointer()`, so after checkpoint recovery stale tail records beyond the recovered pointer must not be replayed into FP-set recovery.
- Model-checker checkpoint recovery rebuilds the FP set from the concurrent worker trace enumerator when `ConcurrentTrace` is active. Java's `trace` field is a `ConcurrentTLCTrace` subclass, so `theFPSet.recover(this.trace)` dispatches to worker-file enumeration rather than the legacy marker/base trace alone.
- No-code audit note: `ModelChecker.doPeriodicWork` scheduling and runtime-ratio math were rechecked against Java. Go keeps Java's early skip/suspend condition, odd equality-at-liveness-ratio suspend/resume behavior, non-resume exits for liveness/periodic failures, checkpoint-owned resume, and progress-interval runtime-ratio approximation. `ForceLivenessCheck` now only flips the checker flag like Java `forceLiveCheck()`.
- Checker and DFID model-check paths must normalize any Go `error` returned with `EC.NO_ERROR` to Java's `EC.GENERAL` before printing failure summaries or deciding cleanup success. Java exceptions in `modelCheckImpl` become non-success results before the `finally` cleanup path, so Go must not let split `(NO_ERROR, err)` returns trigger success cleanup.
- Original `tlc2.REPLTest.testProcessInput` now has all thirteen sequential expressions and exact results translated in root `repl_java_test.go`. Production `REPL.ProcessInput` uses the real parser/tool and Java EXTENDS list `Reals,Sequences,Bags,FiniteSets,TLC,Randomization`, writes CFG before TLA, resets ToolIO to TOOL mode, catches only evaluation/runtime failures, preserves individual SANY error parameters and flushes its buffered PrintWriter before setting TLC output to null. Optional CommunityModules index presence has an explicit native provider; absent or failed optional loading is ignored. The existing `EvaluateREPLExpression` convenience API retains its temporary-directory management and output restoration. `TLC.Print`/`PrintT` use ToolIO when output is null; a non-null writer receives PrintT without an added newline, as in Java. Interactive terminal/history remains separate.
- Java output stream helpers were ported as concrete Go structs: `DelayedPrintStream` buffers writes until `Release` writes, flushes, and resets like Java's delayed print stream; `TeeOutputStream` writes main branch first, then secondary branch, flushes in the same order, and closes the secondary stream even when primary close fails, returning the secondary close error when both fail like Java's `finally` shape.
- No-code audit note: management/JMX-adjacent wrappers were rechecked against Java `ModelCheckerMXWrapper`, `TLCServerMXWrapper`, `TLCStatisticsMXBean`, `TLCStandardMBean`, and `StateMonitor`. Go preserves the MX bean method surface, dirty DiskFPSet distinct-count shortcut, checkpoint/liveness/suspend/resume/stop controls, object-name constants, version/revision fallbacks, and distributed-server `N/A`/`-1` cases. Java `StateMonitor` is attach/JMX console transport plumbing and remains intentionally outside the core checker until a Go monitoring CLI is in scope.
- No-code audit note: trace-expression/spec-writer helpers were rechecked against Java `TraceExpressionExplorerSpecWriter`, `SpecTraceExpressionWriter`, and `AbstractSpecWriter`. Go preserves generated trace-expression variable prefixes, comment-prefix parsing, lexicographic expression-variable ordering, TE init/next identifiers and attributes, config/TLA buffer append order, closing/timestamp behavior, and stuttering/back-to-state trace rewriting.
- Java `tlc2.model` presentation helpers now have their small Java tests mirrored in Go for `Formula`, `Assignment`, and `TypedSet`. `Assignment.SetFormula` is intentionally unsupported in Java and Go; do not treat its `Not implemented yet` panic as a missing TLC core behavior.
- `OffHeapDiskFPSet` eviction is coordinated through a package singleton like Java's `OffHeapSynchronizer`, not independently per child FP set. Any forced/probe-limit eviction must suspend at the shared barrier, evict all registered off-heap sets in insertion order, then clear the shared pending flag. Go unregisters closed off-heap sets to avoid retaining dead file handles; preserve the shared barrier shape, but do not reintroduce the non-load-bearing leak. Off-heap `CheckFPs` deliberately follows Java's approximate in-memory scan and returns `Long.MAX_VALUE` when no unflushed fingerprints remain; do not replace it with the heap-backed exact disk-file scan.
- No-code audit note: `StateQueue`, `MemStateQueue`, and `DiskStateQueue` were rechecked against Java for synchronized enqueue/dequeue, finish/suspend/resume races, checkpoint ordering, queue-growth policy, non-recursive delete behavior, and disk recover/checkpoint field order. Go keeps Java's separate suspend barrier, `finishAll` wake-up of both workers and the checkpoint waiter, and the disk queue's Java-visible recovery/checkpoint oddities.
- DFID periodic work holds the `MemFPIntSet` monitor across liveness checking and checkpointing like Java `DFIDModelChecker.doPeriodicWork`. Keep the private lock-held checkpoint helper separate from public `Checkpoint()` so Go does not deadlock on its non-reentrant mutex while still preserving Java's FP-set/liveness/UniqueString begin/commit ordering.
- Checker result precedence now mirrors Java `AbstractChecker.modelCheck`: if the implementation path returns `NO_ERROR` but `errorCode` was set, the public result falls back to that stored code after cleanup has used the implementation result for its success decision. This matters for kept-call-stack worker errors where `runTLC` returns `NO_ERROR` to allow replay.
- Worker next-state error reports now preserve Java's checker-monitor serialization across error acceptance, diagnostic/trace output, and error-time postconditions. `ModelChecker.nextErrorMu` covers ordinary/evaluation/runtime failures, continuation-mode violation traces, and the worker outer panic report; the postcondition wrapper calls a lock-held helper rather than recursively taking the Go mutex. Keep this lock separate from the checker state mutex so ALIAS/postcondition evaluation can query or control the checker through `TLCGet`/`TLCSet`. The `console` flag reads `Done` under the state mutex while the report lock preserves worker-report ordering. A focused two-worker regression failed before the fix and now verifies serialized postconditions, first-error/continuation precedence, and the first-vs-later counterexample `console` field; it also passes with `-race`.
- No-action checker cleanup mirrors Java `ModelChecker.modelCheckImpl`: when initial states exist but the spec has no `NEXT` action, TLC reports `TLC_STATES_AND_NO_NEXT_ACTION` but still calls `cleanup(true)` once. Do not "fix" this to failure cleanup; Java treats the no-action early-exit branch as success cleanup for metadata deletion purposes.
- Coverage root labels follow Java `ActionWrapper.printLocation`: undeclared actions print the action string, declared one-to-one actions print the declaration location, and declared one-to-many action disjuncts append the actual predicate source range. Do not simplify coverage output back to `Action.getLocation()`, which is used by traces/debug/DOT rather than coverage summaries.
- `Action.getDeclaration()` is not the same source range as `Action.getDefinition()`: Java reads the operator definition's left-hand-side `IdentLHS` tree node for the declaration, while definition/display location comes from the predicate/body semantic node. Go carries a separate parser `Definition.LHSPos` into `OpDefNode.DeclarationLocation`; do not collapse it back into `SemanticNodeBase.Location`.
- No-code audit note: `StatePrinter`, `ErrorTraceMessagePrinterRecorder`, `BroadcastMessagePrinterRecorder`, `CheckImpl`, and `CheckImplFile` were rechecked against Java. Go keeps the same state-print EC codes, diff-only/fingerprint/overwrite behavior, stuttering/back-to-state recorder termination, idempotent recorder subscription semantics, CheckImpl FP-set boolean interpretation, and Java's odd `checkTrace` habit of continuing after false check results unless an actual error is raised.
- `TLCTraceEnumerator.Reset(-1)` preserves the current enumerator position like Java and, for disk traces, refreshes the trace-file length after reopening. Do not turn `-1` into a rewind-to-start helper; Java uses it as "reset at current position."
- No-code audit note: `TLAPlusExecutor`, `TraceApp` reconstruction hooks, `EvalException`, `WorkerException`, `StatefulRuntimeException`, and `FingerprintException` were rechecked against Java. Go preserves executor locking/action mapping/first-state stepping, alias-prefix/suffix reconstruction helpers, EvalException code+parameter carriers, worker predecessor/successor call-stack flags, known-exception toggles, and fingerprint trace source-node collapsing.
- Call-stack replay workers must not mirror replay-generated states into `ModelChecker.Trace`. Java constructs worker id `4223` for replay but explicitly does not add it to the trace worker set; Go preserves that with `Worker.DisableTraceMirror`, while still allowing the synthetic worker's local trace context to assign predecessor pointers during diagnostic reconstruction.
- Liveness call-stack replay preserves Java's "replay succeeded" bug path: if `liveCheck.addNextState` fails in ordinary mode but succeeds under `CallStackTool`, Go now returns a general TLC error like Java `Assert.fail(EC.GENERAL, origExp)` instead of reporting the original liveness error as if replay had failed normally.
- Exploration/debug simulation was rechecked directly against Java `ExplorationWorker`: Go keeps the separate init-state functor, in-model filtering without invariant rechecks, all-successor `Tool.GetNextStatesWithFunctor` path, halt-reset behavior, liveness-before-post-trace ordering, and distinct RL mode precedence. Do not split this back into a second worker type.
- `DebugTableauDiskGraph` parity is now folded into the concrete Go `TableauDiskGraph`: when `tlc2.tool.liveness.LiveCheck.debug=true`, tableau disk mutations write Java-named DOT snapshots after `AddNode`, `SetDone`, and `RecordNode`, using the same cache-create/write/destroy diagnostic path. Do not add a wrapper/interface for this.
- No-code audit note: `BuiltInOPs`, `ToolGlobals` opcode values, `TransitiveClosure.Warshall`, `AnySet`, and built-in module registration were rechecked. Go preserves Java opcode numbers/range predicates, Warshall's insertion-order node list and row-major output, `ANY` comparison/membership/finite/display behavior, and the active built-in module/native override surface represented by `InstallStandardDefinitions`.
- `ASTToLive` follows Java liveness recursive-operator expansion: non-recursive operators still fall back after failed expansion, recursive operators at action-or-lower level are left for normal evaluation, and recursive temporal operators must expand successfully so the tableau sees the temporal structure.
- `Liveness.processLiveness` debug output now mirrors Java's `Boolean.getBoolean("tlc2.tool.liveness.Liveness.debug")` hook, including EC `TLC_LIVE_IMPLIED_DEBUG` and Java's parameter ordering for possible error models, promises, action-bin count, state-bin count, and tableau size.
- No-code audit note: `TLCGlobals`, `Cache`, `List`, and Java `MemBasedSet` were rechecked. Go keeps Java checkpoint/progress/liveness/coverage defaults and edge semantics; `SimpleCache` still mirrors the Java `Cache` contract and sentinel counts; `List` keeps shallow-copy, reference-membership, append/destructive-append behavior; and `MemBasedSet`'s 1.5x growth rule is folded into concrete int-stack/queue ports rather than kept as an extra abstract type.
- No-code audit note: object-stack utilities, `Sx`/`SimpUtil`, and `Combinatorics` were rechecked. Go keeps Java object-stack LIFO/pool/checkpoint behavior while intentionally ignoring the unused broken asynchronous `DiskIntStack` sketch in favor of the already-ported `SynchronousDiskIntStack`; S-expression atoms are interned and printed like Java; combinatorics table generation, big-int conversion, binomial fallback, and Java's quirky `sumChoose(n, n-1)` arithmetic are mirrored.
- `TLCStateMut.Copy`, `DeepCopy`, and `CopyWith` have been re-audited against Java `TLCStateMut`, `TLCStateMutExt`, and base `TLCState.copyWith`. Ordinary copies drop predecessor/action, extended-mode `Copy`/`DeepCopy` preserve predecessor/action, and `CopyWith` only preserves selected variable values plus level, not extended metadata. Do not "fix" `CopyWith` to keep predecessor/action; Java's base `copyWith` calls only the protected level-copy hook.
- Composite value constructors intentionally retain supplied slices like Java retains supplied arrays for `TupleValue`, `RecordValue`, and `FcnRcdValue`. Do not reintroduce defensive copies in those constructors unless deliberately diverging from Java; callers that need ownership must copy before construction, matching Java's call-site responsibility.
- `ValueVec(Value[])` in Java retains the supplied array, so Go `NewValueVecFrom` intentionally retains its supplied slice. This makes `SetEnumValue(Value[])` ownership match Java too.
- Tuple and record `Select` methods intentionally report Java-style type errors for non-integer/non-string selectors instead of returning nil. A nil result is reserved for a well-typed selector that is outside the tuple/record domain.
- `TupleValue` has been re-audited against Java for comparison, equality, selection/application, EXCEPT, domain, normalization, fingerprinting, permutation, and string output. Preserve the Java EXCEPT quirk where an out-of-range integer tuple field returns a new tuple with unfilled slots rather than returning the original tuple.
- `IntervalValue` comparison/equality for non-intervals must convert through `ToSetEnum` like Java instead of calling model-value hooks directly. Membership uses `low <= high` for non-empty checks, so huge intervals do not trigger size-overflow diagnostics for non-integer membership; untyped model values are simple non-members.
- `ModelValue` typed/untyped comparison, equality, non-model hooks, membership errors, fingerprinting, and permutation have been re-audited against Java. Typed model values must still reject non-model comparisons through the same hook methods used by other values.
- Primitive `BoolValue`, `IntValue`, and `StringValue` comparison/equality, model-value hooks, finite/size errors, EXCEPT, fingerprinting, and display have been re-audited against Java. There is no separate Java `RealValue` peer in the current source tree.
- Sentinel `UndefValue` and override-backed `UserValue` have been re-audited against Java for comparison/equality, finite/size errors, EXCEPT, normalization, definition status, fingerprint fallback, and display.
- Operator wrapper values preserve Java's failure behavior for ordinary value operations: `Permute` and fingerprinting must fail through the base unsupported-value path, singular EXCEPT keeps Java's `appy` typo, and normalization uses `Should not normalize an operator.` for `OpLambdaValue`/`OpRcdValue` but `It is a TLC bug: Attempted to normalize an operator.` for Java-method/evaluating wrappers. Operator-record construction now retains backing slices like Java `Vect`s, and application diagnostics use Java capitalization/punctuation, including the Go-only non-operator fallback.
- Java `CallableValue extends EvaluatingValue`; Go now treats callable wrappers as evaluating values for level-bound checks and op-definition cloning while still preserving the callable-specific `EvalWithTool` override. `PriorityEvaluatingValue` already had explicit handling because it aggregates evaluating handles.
- Binary set operation wrappers and `UnionValue` have been re-audited for lazy enumeration, cached real-set conversion, finite checks, EXCEPT diagnostics, and Java's odd set-operation diagnostic spacing. Union has its own EXCEPT messages; do not route it through the binary set helper.
- Set-constructor values (`SetOfTuplesValue`, `SetOfRcdsValue`, `SetOfFcnsValue`, `SubsetValue`, and separate Go `KSubsetValue`) preserve Java's `SetEnumValue.DummyEnum` deep-normalization state with explicit dummy flags. Do not collapse a deep-normalized-but-not-enumerated value back into a plain nil cache. Tuple/record set constructors also retain caller slices like Java retains arrays and record-set sorting mutates those slices in place.
- Lazy set-operation values (`SetCupValue`, `SetCapValue`, `SetDiffValue`, and `UnionValue`) also preserve Java's `SetEnumValue.DummyEnum` deep-normalization sentinel with explicit dummy flags. After `DeepNormalize`, later materialization must deep-normalize the produced `SetEnumValue`; serialization treats dummy caches as still unmaterialized.
- Set-constructor diagnostics now use Java's class-specific EXCEPT, membership, duplicate-field, product-enumeration, and product-size overflow wording instead of the generic set helper for tuple/record/function set values. Random subsets of record sets reuse the record-set field-name slice and construct `RecordValue(..., false)` like Java's `RcdProduct.elementOf`.
- `SubsetValue` now uses Java's non-enumerable membership diagnostic and module-overflow code for powerset size overflow, in addition to the dummy-enum cache behavior noted above.
- `FcnRcdValue` has been re-audited against Java for comparison/equality, interval-domain comparisons, membership/application/select diagnostics, normalization, conversion to tuple/record, fingerprinting, permutation, and display-shape predicates. The implementation was already algorithmically aligned; the latest changes tightened Java-visible diagnostic wording.
- `RecordValue` has been re-audited against Java for comparison/equality, membership/application/select diagnostics, EXCEPT warning payloads, function-record conversion, normalization, deep copy, fingerprinting, permutation, and display. The existing Go test for missing/non-string field diagnostics now expects Java capitalization.
- `FcnLambdaValue` and `FcnParams` have been re-audited against Java for constructor ownership, copy-constructor EXCEPT retention, shallow `ValueExcept` cursor copies, application/select argument diagnostics, domain materialization, tuple/record conversion, normalization, deep normalization, fingerprinting, permutation, and string expansion. `FcnParams` now retains caller slices like Java retains arrays, and its size/enumerability diagnostics use Java message text/codes.
- `Tool.getFcnContext` now has its own Java-shaped binding algorithm instead of reusing `FcnLambdaValue`'s selection helper. It preserves domain-before-tuple validation, per-argument diagnostics (including Java's missing newline before `which` in two branches), the function-expression source suffix, captured-context binding, ignored excess arguments, and direct-index failure for short argument lists. The single tuple-mismatch branch deliberately reports the tool object's identity like Java's `this.toString()` typo, using Go's type/address identity for ordinary tools and the call-stack string for `CallStackTool`'s overridden `toString()`. Focused regressions cover scalar/multiple/mixed tuple binding and failure precedence. `FcnLambdaValue.String` also now catches expansion panics like Java's inner `catch(Throwable)`, so formatting a malformed lazy function falls back to symbolic text instead of replacing the application error with a printing panic.
- `SetPredValue` has been re-audited against Java for converted-set caching, copied state/context construction, membership predicate evaluation, finite checks, EXCEPT behavior, normalization, materialization, permutation/fingerprint delegation, string output, and enumeration. The latest changes tightened Java-visible diagnostics for predicate failures, non-enumerable source sets, and tuple-binding errors.
- `Tool`'s `$SubsetOf` construction now uses Java's `Reducible` boundary: only `IntervalValue` and `SetEnumValue` are eagerly filtered; other values, including enumerable powersets and tuple/function/record products, stay as `SetPredValue`. Do not broaden this branch to every `Enumerable`: that evaluates predicates prematurely and can enumerate enormous spaces during construction. The same concrete `isReducibleValue` helper serves function-domain construction. Focused regressions failed on premature predicate calls before the fix and now verify deferred membership evaluation and captured-state isolation.
- `Tool`'s set difference/intersection/union now dispatch to concrete `IntervalValue`/`SetEnumValue` `Diff`/`Cap`/`Cup` methods like Java `Reducible`. Difference only reduces the left operand; intersection and union prefer the left reducible operand and otherwise reduce the right. Explicit-set methods retain raw left order, duplicates, and normalization flags; union enumerates/normalizes only its reducible right operand and marks the result unnormalized. Empty reducible unions return the other operand unchanged, and lazy unions place the selected reducible operand first. Interval methods validate Java's signed-32-bit size boundary. A frozen local Java probe confirmed all six raw result shapes; focused tests cover those results, non-enumerable membership-only intersection, union identity/order, and overflow.
- Value cost models now live in `BaseValue`, mirroring Java `Value.cm`, with concrete get/set accessors and the existing evaluating/lambda/predicate fields promoted from that base. Set enumeration, interval conversion, lazy binary set operations, lazy union, and lazy set-predicate materialization/enumeration now retain Java's secondary-count boundaries. Explicit-set enumerators count every call, including exhausted calls; intervals count only elements; lazy filters count examined candidates; materialization separately counts returned elements. Reducers preserve Java's model propagation, including explicit-set union's deliberate default model. `Tool` now invokes `UnionValue.union`'s Go helper so explicit sets of explicit sets combine eagerly without normalizing raw input, and both eager/lazy union results inherit the input set's model. This was compared directly to Java source and an already-created local Java probe; no new regression/unit tests were added after the user's instruction. The existing fake value gained only the accessor required by the extended Java-shaped `Value` contract.
- Function-record/lambda conversions and lambda permutation now propagate normalization, domain-size, selection, and materialization failures that Java throws; ordinary shape non-convertibility still returns null. Lambda tuple conversion preserves null element slots. Eager function construction returns a materialization failure instead of silently keeping the lambda lazy. `Tool.Eval`/`EvalAppl` adapt only TLC runtime/evaluation/fingerprint error panics into Go errors, retaining their categories and call-stack handling; unrelated runtime panics propagate. Verified against Java source and the existing full suite; no new tests were written.
- Value-side coverage now also follows Java in product tuple/record/function enumeration, powerset/k-subset materialization, normalized subset elements, and tuple/record/function conversions. Products count generated fields before advancing their enumerators; empty-domain function sets count the sole empty function once. Normalized subset iterators attach the model to generated subsets without adding a generation count. Powerset materialization validates and allocates for its full cardinality before enumeration; zero-sized bases return the singleton empty subset before attempting set conversion. The conversion helper distinguishes Java's null conversion result from an actual materialization error. `Tool` threads models through concrete constructors and subset-assignment wrappers. Preserve two Java conversion quirks: interval-domain `FcnRcdValue.toTuple` drops the model without incrementing, while explicit-domain `FcnLambdaValue.toTuple` increments unconditionally even with coverage disabled.
- Lazy-function materialization now preserves Java's raw tuple casts and fixed declared-size arrays instead of converting tuple-like function elements or truncating partially filled arrays. Its cached function record receives the original model, and the materialization count is incremented after cache installation but before EXCEPT updates. Product and parameter iterators stop before returning a saved element when advancing the next position fails, matching Java's thrown-exception boundary. The preexisting `FcnParams` tuple-group `enums[i]` initialization quirk remains intact. These changes were checked against Java source and the existing Go suite; no new tests were written.
- Cleanup rule: do not preserve Java's likely early-return resource leak, but do preserve the load-bearing `FileUtil.deleteDir(metadir, success)` behavior and explicit-checkpoint recovery veto. When checker cleanup is called with `success=false`, it must close resources while keeping non-empty metadata/artifact directories; when called with `success=true`, it may recursively remove them unless a non-empty explicit-checkpoint run is being snapshotted for recovery. See `TestModelCheckerCleanupPreservesFailureArtifactsLikeJava` and `TestModelCheckerCleanupSnapshotsRecoverableRunAndStillClosesResources`.
- Runner `-cleanup` rule: Java TLC's command-line `-cleanup` pre-cleans the metadata directory before a non-recovery run; it does not control the checker finally cleanup. Keep Go runner cleanup flags separate from `ModelChecker.cleanup(success)`, which remains Java-shaped and enabled unless the veto property blocks deletion. This separation is load-bearing: stale checkpoint state must be removable before a fresh run, but `Cleanup=false` at the runner must not leak successful checker metadata. See `TestTLCRunnerCleanupFlagPrecleanIsSeparateFromCheckerFinalCleanup`.
- Runner command-line metadir setup mirrors Java `FileUtil.makeMetaDir`: parsed CLI runs create a timestamped child of `states` or the explicit `-metadir` root, `-recover` uses the checkpoint directory directly, `${metadir}` dump paths are resolved after that final directory exists, and CLI `-cleanup` is marked as already pre-cleaned so `Process` does not delete the fresh timestamped directory. Programmatic `NewTLC(Options{MetaDir: ...})` still treats `MetaDir` as the final checker directory.
- Runner `-generateSpecTE` forces trace-spec generation but does not imply `-tool`. Java still emits ordinary CLI timing/output unless `-tool` is explicitly present or the jar-contained model fallback enables it.
- Runner `-userFile` now opens/truncates the output file during CLI parameter parsing, routes `TLC!Print`/`PrintT` to it while `Process` runs, and closes/restores that output before the finished banner. Preserve Java's quirky `PrintT` behavior: stdout gets a println newline, user-file output uses the direct writer path without adding that extra newline.
- Runner `-debugger` now installs a concrete Go analogue of Java `DebugTool`: `Process` attaches a `TLCDebugger`, switches the tool to `ModeDebugger`, preserves `port=0` as an explicitly requested debugger port, keeps a fast debugger-free shallow tool for `Tool.NoDebug()`, and routes const/state/action evaluation through `DebugEvalMode` frame pushes while bypassing debugger-triggered, liveness, `ENABLED`, primed, and leaf-token evaluations like Java. The public init/next-state debugger frames, protected init/next application frames, state-functor wrapping, unsatisfied-state hooks, `UNCHANGED` exception frames, reset/abort next-state retry shape, and MC-debug predecessor cleanup are in place. Remaining debugger parity work should focus on DAP transport/event behavior and any later Java `TLCDebuggerTestCase` details, not the `DebugTool` attachment/evaluation skeleton.
- Debugger stack-trace request behavior now mirrors Java `TLCDebugger.stackTrace`: stack frames are hidden while execution is not halted, synthetic trace frames are reconstructed lazily only when requested, simulator traces use `GetUncompressedTrace`, model-checker traces combine predecessor suffixes with `ModelChecker.GetTraceInfo`, request pagination follows `startFrame`/`levels`, and continue/step/reverse/goto/disconnect commands clear the virtual trace frames and mark execution as resumed. Do not move synthetic trace-frame construction into `HaltExecution`; Java deliberately avoids retaining those frames unless the frontend asks for them.
- Debugger initialize capability reporting now mirrors Java `TLCDebugger.initialize` as plain Go structs: goto-state is tied to simulator presence; hover/evaluate, terminate, exception filter options, hit-conditional/conditional breakpoints, step-back, and clipboard context are enabled; exception-info, log points, value formatting, stepping granularity, goto-targets, data/function/instruction breakpoints, and disassembly remain disabled.
- Debugger's small request helpers now match Java's no-transport behavior: `threads` reports a single `worker` thread with id `0`, `setVariable` returns an empty response, `configurationDone` is a no-op, and `TerminateCommand` stops the active checker/simulator before reusing disconnect cleanup.
- Debugger conditional breakpoints now keep Java's null-condition behavior: parse/semantic failures are reported on the breakpoint response, but a missing compiled condition op does not suppress a later source-location match.
- Debugger source-breakpoint verification now mirrors Java's response behavior: breakpoints are stored regardless of verification, verified status is computed by a fuzzy semantic-location walk, non-spec modules stay verified like Java's `moduleNode == null` case, condition parse errors only mark known-module breakpoints unverified, and hit conditions on the configured `Next` predicate are rejected with Java's response message. Go walks processed definitions instead of a retained SANY `ModuleNode`, but keeps Java `Location.includes` range logic and the odd breakpoint range with begin line `line + 1` and end line `line`.
- Output control mirrors Java `MP` recorder ordering: suppression and `-nowarning` now mark `Message.Suppressed` instead of dropping recorder events, `PrintError` ignores suppression like Java, and `-messagesAsErrors` aborts `PrintWarning` through Java Assert.fail runtime failures, recording a formatting-only MP.getMessage event before throwing (corrected in the distributed init audit). `TLCExt!PickSuccessor` prompt/status output also goes through `TLC_MODULE_OVERRIDE_STDOUT`/`PrintMessage`, not direct stdout writes.
- Trace exploration binary setup now mirrors Java's pre-tool construction path: `-generateSpecTE` derives/stores the TE module name during option finalization, appends the implicit `_TLCTrace!_TLCTraceSilent` runtime postcondition when binary generation is enabled, and reuses the same module name during final TE `.tla` generation.
- Trace exploration generated TE constants now use the processed `Defns` table like Java `TraceExplorationSpec`, not just raw config declarations. This preserves the Java distinction between model values already defined by the processed spec and model values that must be reified in the generated `TEConstants` module.
- Trace exploration variables now come only from the global TLC state-variable list, mirroring Java `TLCState.Empty.getVarsAsStrings()`. Do not derive a fallback variable list from `MCError` trace states; that produces friendlier output but diverges from Java's TE spec generator.
- Runtime postconditions may deliberately target module-qualified LOCAL standard definitions. The bridge indexes every parsed definition under `Module!Name` while still keeping extended LOCAL definitions out of the unqualified/named-instance export surface, so `_TLCTrace!_TLCTraceSilent` is valid for the Java trace-exploration binary hook but `_TLCTraceSilent` remains unexported. See `TestRuntimePostConditionCanTargetQualifiedLocalStandardDefinition`.
- Root `modelcheck -go-tlc` warning controls now split like Java TLC: `-suppressMessages`/`-messagesAsErrors` still flow into the TLC runtime, while known SANY diagnostic codes are also applied to parse/semantic/bridge diagnostics without rejecting TLC-only numeric codes.
- TLC command-line message-code validation mirrors Java `EC.isKnownCode` plus SANY standardized `ErrorCode` values. Do not return to accepting arbitrary numeric `-suppressMessages`/`-messagesAsErrors` entries; Java rejects unknown codes at parse time.
- TLC command-line suppression also mirrors Java's SANY severity rule: standardized SANY warning codes `4800` through `4805` may be suppressed, but standardized SANY error codes such as `4200` are rejected for `-suppressMessages`. `-messagesAsErrors` still accepts any known TLC or SANY code, matching Java's classify path.
- No-code audit note: `ParseTLCOptions` was rechecked against current Java `TLC.handleParameters`. The Go path covers Java's visible flags, including case-insensitive `-loadTrace`/`-dumpTrace`/`-postCondition`, runtime invariant module extraction, trace-spec binary postcondition setup, `-teSpecOutDir` file-vs-directory naming, cleanup/metadir/recover path setup, and FP/fpmem/fpbits validation. Java currently consumes `-generateSpecTE nomonolith` without storing a parser-side boolean; Go's `GenerateTraceSpecMonolith` field is inert downstream and should not be treated as an active divergence unless trace-spec writing grows a real monolith switch.
- `TLCExt!TLCEvalDefinition` now reports non-zero-arity definition errors with the Java `OpDefNode.getSignature()` shape (`Name(p, q)`) rather than the bare operator name.
- Symbol lookup hazard: Java `SymbolNodeValueLookupProvider.lookup` uses the queried symbol itself as a "not found" sentinel, consults context/tool objects before state lookup, and deliberately avoids state lookup for user-defined operators (GitHub #362 name-clash fix). Go now marks TLC symbols as state-variable declarations or user-defined operators; `Tool.LookupWithCutoff` skips state lookup for user-defined-operator symbols after checking direct and name-based definitions, while `GetVar`/primed-location/incomplete-state paths require actual variable-declaration symbols. Do not remove this kind metadata or reorder lookup back to state-first.
- `LazyValue`, `SetPredValue`, and `FcnLambdaValue` now carry Java's source-sensitive catch boundaries. Lazy-function materialization's catch lives on the concrete Go materialization helper representing Java `toFcnRcd`, so pointer conversions do not add an extra head. Set-predicate membership now rewrites only direct EvalException carriers in its inner catch, including domain/binding failures, then applies outer source wrapping; ordinary runtime and fingerprint errors survive. Membership uses Java's no-cost-model evaluator overload, while predicate enumeration retains its model. Predicate permutation propagates materialization failures, and checked predicate printing swallows expansion panics before symbolic fallback. Lazy deep normalization is the inherited Java no-op, and direct lazy evaluation threads its stored model. Existing checks pass with the mixed-set config-printing test excluded; no tests were added or modified.
- Tuple, record, and finite-function methods now preserve Java's sourced failure chains for comparison, membership, application/selection, EXCEPT, domain, normalization, definition checks, copying, fingerprinting, permutation, and printing. Record/function normalization helpers carry the Java `normalize` catch boundary; pointer-returning callers propagate failures instead of ignoring them. The interval-size helper used by function equality and tuple-shaped printing now throws on size overflow rather than interpreting it as size zero. Go exception `Error()` follows linked heads to the root cause before formatting a failed value, preventing secondary printing failures from masking the original error. Existing checks pass with the documented mixed-set config-printing test excluded; no tests were written or modified.
- Value-side source-sensitive catches are now ported for booleans, integers, strings, explicit sets, and intervals, including reducers and the shared hash/empty/subset helpers. Returned errors gain one `FingerprintException` head per Java catch boundary; pointer/fingerprint operations rethrow as panics, and unsourced values retain their original failures. Explicit-set normalization errors now propagate through normalization, deep normalization, fingerprinting, printing, tuple conversion, and comparison conversion instead of being discarded. Exception traces read each value's current source like Java instead of capturing it at exception construction, and `asTrace` retains null source entries.
- Subset helper architecture is now ported in `value_subset_helpers.go`: `GetUnrank`/`SubsetUnrank.SubsetAt` preserve Java’s strict TreeMap predecessor/cache behavior using sorted cutoffs, Pascal-table lookup, exact long conversions, descending element insertion, and outer cost-model reference. `GetRandomSetOfSubsetsUpTo` ports the integer overload with scale-32 HALF_DOWN decimal rounding, per-rank bias, signed-long stride/Math.abs behavior, and allocation/random-consumption/failure order; keep its Java zero-modulus and invalid-rank behavior rather than adding guards. Fixed-cardinality `NumberOfKElements`, `KElements`, bounded `KElementEnumeration` (including reset/sort/asSet), and `KSubset` are represented; ordinary k-subset traversal now takes Java’s int-count limit, while ordinary powerset combinations remain unbounded. Lexicographic traversal preserves constructor mutation of the outer set and coverage counts. Empty enumeration constructs a fresh normalized empty set after reset. All inherited helpers retain the concrete k-subset receiver/model too.
- Randomization’s probability branch now delegates to the shared subset helper with Java’s double-to-int cast, per-element generator lookup, conversion failure boundary, and duplicate suppression. Hash-set equality failures propagate rather than being ignored. `ValueVec` and random hash-set negative capacities now fail like Java instead of becoming zero; negative `RandomSubset` allocation errors are runtime override failures rather than evaluation carriers. Existing checks pass with the documented mixed-set config test skipped; no tests were added or modified. New helper behavior was ported from source and compiled; dedicated behavioral tests remain deferred by the user. Existing hash-set output retains deterministic first-insertion order; a later Java HashSet bucket-order audit remains separate.
- Distributed failure classification now uses concrete `RemoteException`, `ServerException`, `EOFException`, `OutOfMemoryError`, `RejectedExecutionException`, and `NullPointerException` carriers instead of the artificial `DistributedRecoverableError` marker. Nullable messages, causes, Java class names, and saved Go frames remain available; RemoteException preserves its special public-detail cause and nested-exception message. The worker rethrows only direct WorkerExceptions, converts direct out-of-memory/executor-rejection failures to distinct remote exceptions, and wraps other failures as WorkerException. The local smart proxy preserves RMI's ServerException envelope so the server's exact one/two-level recoverability predicate works without adding networking. EOF with an empty message does not qualify, wrapped evaluation/fingerprint causes are not searched recursively, and non-remote/non-NPE failures use the outer GENERAL/model-error path rather than deregistering a worker. NPE worker-loss messages carry the stack trace, and recoverable-block messages precede requeue/limit updates like Java. The JDK RemoteException/ServerException and UnicastServerRef behavior was inspected with local `javap`; no tests were authored or modified in this pass. Full existing checks pass in the working tree, which also contains a separately pending mixed-set config-test expectation correction. Remaining transport work includes networking/lifecycle shells, additional RMI error subclasses, and Java URI ASCII/NFC handling for worker metadata; legacy TLCError family tagging and nested checked/unchecked value strings remain pending.
- Smart-proxy and worker computation timing now subtract epoch millisecond timestamps like Java System.currentTimeMillis instead of truncating Go monotonic elapsed durations. Empty proxy blocks retain Java's floating-point division by zero (positive infinity for the normal timing path) rather than substituting a one-state denominator. Signed-long sanitization already matched Java and was retained.
- Nullable Throwable detail messages and exception stack representation are now carried in `throwable.go`. Ported fingerprint/stateful/worker/evaluation/config/liveness/TLC carriers expose `GetMessage() *string`; empty strings remain non-null, fingerprint heads always have a null message, and a worker wrapper copies the caught Throwable's nullable message without replacing it with the cause text. ConfigFileException retains its constructor-formatted detail message. Constructors capture Go runtime frames; stack rendering preserves Java class names for represented exception families, common-frame elision and circular causes, and follows the actual cause field (a fingerprint `next` head is not a Throwable cause). Foreign Go error types and frame paths stay Go-native. GENERAL diagnostics preserve Java's runtime-class disguise, append stack traces for null messages, and use MP's historical `noDebug` startup property for the optional non-null-message stack suffix.
- Nullable diagnostic parameters now have an explicit representation (`Message.NullableParams`, evaluation/native carrier fields, and `PrintErrorNullable`). Formatting performs Java's sequential repeated placeholder replacement and stops at the first null parameter while recorder metadata retains the full array. Native evaluating/callable catches preserve a null detail parameter instead of a literal "null"; MethodValue alone replaces a null message with the saved Throwable stack. BFS init/property errors use message-or-toString only for null messages, BFS GENERAL next-error printing is suppressed for all null-message throwables, fingerprint replay passes the root's nullable detail message, and DFID init/assumption/postcondition paths retain null parameters. Direct system-error carriers no longer enter EvalException or TLCRuntimeException classifications. Existing checks pass with the documented mixed-set config test skipped; no tests were written or modified. Remaining exception work: Java RMI-specific transport and explicit family tagging at older TLCError construction sites; detailed nested checked/unchecked value strings remain pending.
- Simulation invariant/action evaluation failures now follow Java SimulationWorker's dedicated error constructor: preserve the property name plus nullable caught detail message, leave the fatal exception field empty, and print the dedicated evaluation-failed code/trace rather than reclassifying it as GENERAL. Simulator/runner runtime printing also preserves nullable override parameters. SimulationWorkerError's GetMessage formats its own code/parameters like Java.
- Remaining direct-exception consumers are now represented: debugger reset/abort checks and known flags, distributed worker reuse/recoverable marker checks, distributed init's invariant escape, and the local worker callback wrapper use the thrown concrete error itself. Debugger evaluation exception frames are limited to Java's EvalException/TLCRuntimeException catch; `TLCError` carries the inherited known bit, and debugger exception pushes mark each exception once like Java. Distributed `GetNextStates` now has the broad outer failure boundary across generation, fingerprinting, routing, and state checks, reuses only directly thrown WorkerExceptions, wraps other errors/panics with current state metadata, and clears the computing flag on every exit. Its successor error field is assigned only in the later state-check phase like Java, not during early fingerprinting. Server errors preserve typed panics, print GENERAL for failures without predecessor metadata, and catch Exception-style trace-print failures before finishing the queue. Existing checks pass with the known mixed-set config test skipped; no tests were written or modified. Java RMI-specific remote/OutOfMemory/RejectedExecution exception transport remains separate from the current recoverable-error marker abstraction; nullable Throwable detail messages, stack rendering, and legacy TLCError family tagging still need a focused representation pass.
- Exception consumers now classify the directly thrown error, matching Java catches/`instanceof`, rather than searching fingerprint/stateful/worker causes. This covers BFS init/next diagnostics and replay, init abort control, call-stack freezing, liveness replay/worker reporting, DFID failure handling, simulator result reporting/stopping, and runner processing. Go explicitly recognizes both liveness concrete classes to preserve Java inheritance; simulation counterexample reuse is restricted to the directly thrown `LiveCounterExampleException`, including its nullable payload. Simulator runtime failures overwrite the worker code and use the runtime parameters; EvalExceptions and fingerprint failures report GENERAL. `TLC.process` likewise has no EvalException catch. Actual EvalExceptions with heap/stack numeric codes remain evaluation exceptions; the existing direct unparameterized system TLCError carriers retain their separate system-failure handling. Existing checks pass with the documented mixed-set config test skipped; no tests were added or modified. Remaining classification audit: debugger and distributed consumers, plus the intentional worker callback wrapper. Remaining representation audit: nullable Throwable detail messages/stack rendering and legacy TLCError sites whose Java runtime-versus-evaluation family has not yet been explicitly carried.
- Native invocation failure boundaries are now ported: `MethodValue.eval` preserves direct EvalException/legacy native evaluation carriers, converts null-pointer panics to override EvalExceptions, rewrites other failures to override runtime errors (including Java’s no-message stack fallback), then applies its outer source catch. `EvaluatingValue` and priority wrappers catch invocation plus fallback broadly with no outer source wrapper; callable argument evaluation remains outside its broad invocation/state-assignment catch. Nil implementations/fallback targets fail instead of silently yielding undefined. Evaluating constructor built-in rejection is ported; callable construction uses Java’s protected bypass. `TLCError.Runtime` distinguishes newly ported TLCRuntime override failures from legacy EvalException carriers, preventing set-predicate membership from rewriting runtime failures. BFS next-failure handling now keeps runtime overrides as GENERAL and treats directly thrown fingerprint errors as GENERAL with a suppressed null-message print rather than inspecting their causes. Existing checks pass with the documented mixed-set config test skipped; no tests were added or modified. Continue checking direct-exception versus cause-chain classification at remaining consumers; detailed checked/unchecked string APIs remain pending. Go uses its own native stack frames for Java’s null-message stack fallback.
- Shared operator-value methods now keep a concrete receiver reference for Java-style dynamic diagnostics, fingerprint/permutation failure heads, source wrapping, and inherited copying. Operator-record diagnostics therefore render the actual record; lambda printing reads the current definition name. Method/evaluating compare/equality/membership diagnostics retain Java’s ternary-precedence quirk (the prefix concatenation is evaluated but omitted), including null-argument failure behavior. Normalization throws a plain wrong-invocation-style runtime error. Priority wrappers now retain primary method metadata and their own source/model while stably sorting handles; op-definition clones retarget receiver references and retain the primary metadata. Native method/evaluating initialization skips unsupported fingerprinting like Java. Existing checks pass with the documented mixed-set config test skipped; no tests were added or modified. Checked/unchecked nested printing and remaining exception-consumer classification remain pending.
- Operator-specific audit: `OpLambdaValue.eval` and `OpRcdValue` application, line addition, definition checks, and printing now preserve source-aware Java catch boundaries. Operator lambdas use Java’s no-cost-model evaluator overload even when the value carries a model. Operator records inherit the default no-op `deepNormalize`; do not normalize their stored arguments/results. Malformed short `addLine` vectors now fail at allocation like Java instead of being silently discarded. Existing checks pass with the documented config mixed-set skip; no tests were added or modified. Native invocation adapters now carry their distinct Java broad/outer catch policies (see newer notes). Detailed checked/unchecked nested string APIs remain pending.
- Model, undefined, and user values now preserve Java’s source-aware exception boundaries, including model-value comparison/membership helpers and the separate inherited default fingerprint/permutation failures. K-subsets now carry their own and inherited catches, preserve the actual receiver/source when delegating membership, and retain the extra inherited subset-equality catch around naive enumeration. K-subset printing swallows only the expansion-size probe, keeps symbolic output when expansion is disabled, and propagates materialization failures; overflow remains a plain runtime-style error like Java’s `IllegalArgumentException`. Cardinality comparison now short-circuits finiteness probes and uses Java’s integer comparator result. Function-set enumeration preserves a domain materialization failure rather than rewriting it as a non-enumerable-domain diagnostic. Existing checks pass with the known mixed-set config test skipped; no tests were added or modified. Nested checked/unchecked string APIs and remaining exception-consumer classification remain pending.
- Lazy set-constructor/operator catches now mirror Java for `SetOfTuplesValue`, `SetOfRcdsValue`, `SetOfFcnsValue`, `SubsetValue`, cup/cap/difference, and `UnionValue`. Returned errors and panics retain source-aware fingerprint chains; fingerprint/permutation conversion failures propagate instead of returning identities. Enumeration wraps only failures present at construction, leaving later iterator failures outside the `elements()` catch. Materialization checks normalization after traversal/coverage accounting like Java. Product printers swallow eligibility/materialization failures but propagate expanded-set printing failures; cup/cap/difference swallow both; UNION and powersets propagate expansion failures. Symbolic interval powersets print `SUBSET (a..b)`, and function-set print expansion uses Java’s long-size loop rather than the overflow-checked public size method. No tests were added or modified; existing checks pass with the known config mixed-set test skipped. Remaining value work includes detailed nested string formatting and exception-consumer classification.
- The earlier mixed-set config test mismatch is resolved: Java `ModelConfig.parseValue` creates an unnormalized set, and Java `SetEnumValue.toString` normalizes it, throwing on its incomparable primitive types. `TestModelConfigParsesConstantsOverridesAndModuleScopes` now verifies the parsed elements and expected printing failure. The full existing suite passes without a skip; preserve the Java behavior.
- `Tool.setSource` now mirrors Java's concrete tool split: ordinary/fast and debugger tools leave values untouched, while call-stack replay overwrites the source at the Java constructor, set-operation, `DOMAIN`/`UNION`, operator-argument, and subset-assignment sites. Function lambdas receive their source before recursive binding/eager materialization. Keep Java's subsequent lambda/predicate copy constructors separate: they deliberately drop the copied value's source. Call-stack freezing now catches only TLC runtime/evaluation/fingerprint errors instead of every returned Go error. Verified against Java and the existing full suite without adding tests. Primitive, explicit-set, tuple, record, and finite-function catch boundaries are ported; remaining checked/unchecked string boundaries are pending.
- LazyValue source attachment now mirrors Java: `BaseValue` carries a source semantic node, and `LazyValue`/`LazySupplierValue` attach the lazy expression to evaluated values that do not already have a source. This feeds debugger display and fingerprint exception traces through the same value-source hook Java uses.
- Unreduced `LazyValue` operations use Java's operation-specific diagnostics, and `Permute` must fail rather than silently returning the lazy value.
- `LazySupplierValue extends LazyValue` in Java; Go now routes supplier values through the same lazy lookup/decomposition paths for eval, init/next predicate processing, config spec/property processing, `UNCHANGED`/`ENABLED`, primed-location collection, and level analysis. Keep the concrete helper functions instead of introducing a one-implementation interface.
- SpecProcessor config decomposition has been re-audited against Java `processConfigSpec`/`processConfigProps`: parameterized inlining uses non-cacheable `getOpContext` lazy bindings, recursive operator defs are skipped, temporal quantifiers and duplicate next-state relations are config errors, empty universal-property enumerators report `TLC_LIVE_FORMULA_TAUTOLOGY`, and action-level `PROPERTY` formulas report Java's specialized property errors instead of becoming implied actions.
- Config/API parity note: Java `Spec.hasAlias()` is based on whether the config names an alias, not whether alias resolution has already produced a semantic node. Go `Tool.HasAlias()` now follows that name-based rule. Config `PROPERTY` entries that name state-level formulas also emit Java's `TLC_LIVE_FORMULA_STATE_LEVEL` warning before being checked as initial-state properties.
- `TLCExt!Trace` and `TLCExt!CounterExample` presence is tied to real SANY-loaded TLCExt definitions, not the globally installed synthetic standard operators. Java injects ALIAS prefix `Trace` only when the external module table contains TLCExt, and Java postcondition counterexamples are bound only when `getCounterExampleDef()` finds the real operator definition. Go now caches those real definitions during the bridge's native-override installation; do not restore a fallback that makes every `Tool` look like it imported TLCExt.
- Invariant config warnings now mirror Java's constant-level branch: a constant `TRUE` invariant is accepted with `TLC_INVARIANT_CONSTANT_LEVEL`, while non-state invariants use the Java `TLC_INVARIANT_VIOLATED_LEVEL` text including the optional level-parameter warning.
- Spec/property liveness warning parity: temporal actions reached through `SPECIFICATION` decomposition are tagged when they originate from a configured `PROPERTY`, enabling Java's `TLC_LIVE_FORMULA_AND_FAIRNESS_TAUTOLOGY` warning for the simple `S /\ L => L` tautology shape. Locations still fall back to body text when parser source spans are unavailable.
- SpecProcessor lifecycle parity: `NewSpecProcessor` no longer runs config processing before the parser bridge has populated variables/definitions. Config processing now happens in the Java-shaped `ApplyToTool` phase, avoiding duplicate warning side effects and premature empty-definition classification.
- Tool predicate validation now reports Java's `TLC_EXPECTED_VALUE` text for non-boolean predicate results. Assumption and postcondition checks still wrap that inner message with their Java evaluation-error codes.
- Checker trace-info forwarding now mirrors Java `ModelChecker.getTraceInfo`: callers can ask the checker for one-state or from/to trace info instead of reaching into trace internals. The base trace fallback now also preserves Java `ConcurrentTLCTrace` segment shape: one-state traces include only an initial destination and otherwise exclude the queried non-initial destination; initial/equal from-to traces return the destination only, while nontrivial from-to traces exclude the destination state.
- No-code audit note: `PossibleAction`, postcondition validity, initial/successor trace reconstruction, symmetry setup, `TLAPlusExecutor`, and `EvalControl` were rechecked against Java and already follow the Java-visible behavior in the Go architecture. `PartialBoolean` now also fails loudly for invalid values instead of silently treating them like `MAYBE`, matching Java's unreachable enum default behavior.
- `CheckImpl` must use Java base `TLCTrace.writeState(predecessor, fp)` semantics when recording externally supplied states. That path writes the trace pointer/fingerprint and updates only the state's trace UID; it must not attach predecessor/action metadata like ordinary model-checker worker traces, because the first external state is checked with `curState == state`.
- Simulation worker errors now build postcondition counterexamples through the Java `SimulationWorkerError.getTrace()` shape: each state is wrapped with its action, aliases are evaluated against the successor state, and liveness-provided counterexamples still win. This keeps printed traces and `TLCExt!CounterExample` postconditions aligned.
- Simulation random-action selection now handles zero enabled/configured actions explicitly before choosing a random action index. Java's `(int)(NaN)` edge falls through to the same deadlock/no-deadlock branch; Go must not rely on NaN-to-int conversion.
- RL reward evaluation now uses Java's `TLC_EXPECTED_VALUE` diagnostic when `_RL_REWARD` evaluates to a non-integer. The ordinary reward evaluation error still escapes through the Java-shaped simulator worker exception boundary.
- No-code audit note: simulator action-flow graph output, simulation trace routing, finite-stutter trace compression, and simulator local register aggregation were rechecked against Java. Go keeps Java hash-code cluster IDs for DOT output but uses deterministic insertion-order maps for stable output.
- `OrderOfSolution` construction now preserves Java's non-null empty-promise-array shape for no-tableau liveness solutions. PEM ordering, duplicate binning, stuttering satisfaction, and debug string composition were rechecked against Java's `Liveness.processLiveness`, `OrderOfSolution`, and `PossibleErrorModel`.
- Liveness expression equality and binaryization now mirror Java's constructor split: `LNState`/`LNAction` equality is tag-only, while `makeBinary` uses raw two-child junction construction so balanced tableau trees are not flattened by `addConj`/`addDisj`.
- Periodic liveness scheduling must preserve Java's raw floating-point edge behavior. The trigger delta uses `(current-last)/(last*1.d)`, so do not add a divide-by-zero guard: `last=0,current>0` deliberately produces `+Inf` and triggers the first partial check, while `0/0` produces `NaN` and does not trigger. `ModelChecker.updateRuntimeRatio` likewise does not clamp a zero denominator; keep Java's possible `NaN`/`Inf` result.
- Progress speed reporting uses Java's double-to-long cast behavior. Do not clamp tiny/zero/negative factors to a friendly value; Java casts `NaN` to `0`, saturates infinities/out-of-range values, and truncates finite doubles toward zero.
- No-code audit note: Java `TraceApp`, `ExplorationWorker`, `ToolGlobals`, `TLCStateVec`, `OpDefEvaluator`, and `FastTool` were checked during the missing-class sweep. Go intentionally folds these into concrete `Tool` state/alias helpers, debugger-mode `SimulateExplorationTrace`, semantic/operator constants, `StateVec`, Tool eval/context methods, and the single concrete Tool path. Java `DebugTool` remains the broader debugger-interception surface and should not be treated as core local checker parity work.
- Simulator aril handling mirrors Java's split behavior: cached `TLCGet("config").aril` remains `"0"` because Java builds the config before `Simulator.simulate()` copies `rng.getAril()`, while the printed simulator summary uses the RNG aril after `setSeed(seed, aril)` normalization. Negative CLI aril therefore prints as `0`, not the raw negative value.
- Direct init/next/ENABLED predicate continuations now report Java's `TLC_EXPECTED_EXPRESSION_IN_COMPUTING` diagnostics for non-boolean results.
